description: Nvidia letter of intent to invest up to $100B in OpenAI, staged against gigawatt-scale deployments of Nvidia systems.
exposure_note: The canonical circular-financing edge: the supplier funds the customer that buys its chips. Bulls call it demand visibility; bears call it vendor financing that flatters reported demand.

description: OpenAI compute commitment to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, the single largest cloud contract ever disclosed.
exposure_note: Drove Oracle's RPO step-change. Concentrates an enormous share of Oracle's backlog in one unprofitable private counterparty — the key bear point on ORCL.

description: Microsoft's cumulative investment in OpenAI, restructured in 2025 into a ~27% stake in the OpenAI Group PBC.
exposure_note: Microsoft books its share of OpenAI losses; the Azure commitment flows back as revenue. Money and compute move in a loop between the two.

description: OpenAI incremental Azure purchase commitment agreed alongside the 2025 restructuring.
exposure_note: Closes the Microsoft-OpenAI loop: investment out, compute revenue back in. Inflates Azure bookings with capital Microsoft itself supplied.

description: Microsoft was CoreWeave's largest customer at roughly 62% of 2024 revenue and about 67% into mid-2026.
exposure_note: CoreWeave's defining risk. Any Microsoft capacity pullback hits ~2/3 of revenue, which is why the Meta, OpenAI and Anthropic wins matter more than their headline value.

description: Meta committed an additional $21B of spend with CoreWeave, disclosed alongside CoreWeave's Q2 2026 results.
exposure_note: Meaningful de-risking of CoreWeave's Microsoft concentration, and evidence Meta is renting rather than building for marginal capacity.

description: Multi-year CoreWeave capacity agreement with Anthropic announced with Q2 2026 results.
exposure_note: Anthropic multi-sourcing compute across AWS, Google and now neoclouds rather than binding to one hyperscaler.

description: Amazon's cumulative investment in Anthropic, with AWS as primary training partner and Trainium as a training platform.
exposure_note: Mirror of the Microsoft-OpenAI structure. Capital out, AWS compute revenue back in, plus a hedge against Nvidia via Trainium.

description: Alphabet investment in Anthropic alongside a large Google Cloud TPU capacity arrangement.
exposure_note: Anthropic is simultaneously a Google Cloud customer and a competitor to Gemini — the sharpest coopetition edge on the map.

description: TSMC manufactures Nvidia's data-center GPUs on leading-edge nodes with CoWoS advanced packaging.
exposure_note: Read-across: TSMC monthly revenue and CoWoS capacity commentary lead Nvidia's shipments. A TSMC packaging constraint caps Nvidia units regardless of demand.

description: TSMC fabricates Broadcom's custom accelerators and switching silicon.
exposure_note: Broadcom competes with Nvidia for the same TSMC leading-edge and CoWoS allocation — they are rivals for supply, not just for customers.

description: TSMC fabricates AMD's Instinct accelerators and EPYC CPUs.
exposure_note: AMD's ability to take GPU share is gated by the TSMC allocation it can secure, not only by product competitiveness.

description: ASML is the sole supplier of EUV lithography systems used for TSMC's leading-edge nodes.
exposure_note: The deepest dependency in the stack. ASML shipment timing sets the ceiling on leading-edge capacity roughly two years out, and is a direct instrument of export control.

description: Micron supplies HBM into Nvidia accelerator platforms; HBM output is sold out through 2026.
exposure_note: HBM attach is the binding input on GPU shipments. Micron's 84.6% gross margin is the clearest evidence of how tight this is — and a direct cost headwind to Nvidia's own margin.

description: Broadcom co-designs and supplies Google's TPU accelerators.
exposure_note: The main escape route from Nvidia. Every TPU generation that works is share that never reaches the merchant GPU market — bearish NVDA, bullish AVGO.

description: 20-year PPA to restart Three Mile Island Unit 1 (Crane Clean Energy Center) for Microsoft data centers.
exposure_note: Template for nuclear-backed AI power. Establishes that hyperscalers will underwrite generation directly when the grid cannot deliver.

description: Susquehanna nuclear co-location supplying an AWS data center campus behind the meter.
exposure_note: Behind-the-meter siting sidesteps the interconnection queue — the single largest scheduling constraint on new AI capacity.

description: Vertiv supplies liquid cooling and power distribution into high-density GPU deployments.
exposure_note: Vertiv orders lead neocloud and hyperscaler capacity by roughly two to four quarters — one of the better early indicators on the whole build-out.

description: Nvidia supplies the GPU fleet CoreWeave rents out, and has also held an equity stake and backstop arrangements.
exposure_note: Second circular-financing edge: Nvidia supplies, invests in, and has contracted capacity from the same counterparty.

description: Dell integrates Nvidia GPUs into AI server and rack-scale systems.
exposure_note: Explains the margin waterfall directly: Dell moves the same AI dollars at 17.8% gross margin because the value sits in the chip it resells.

description: Supermicro builds Nvidia-based AI systems, typically first to market on new platforms.
exposure_note: Allocation-dependent. Supermicro's growth is a function of the GPU supply Nvidia chooses to route through it.

description: Meta is a long-standing large Arista customer for AI back-end Ethernet fabrics.
exposure_note: Arista carries real concentration in Meta and Microsoft. Both are also candidates to shift toward white-box switching, which is the structural bear case.

description: Reddit content licensing agreement with Google for model training and search grounding.
exposure_note: Prices human-generated conversational data. High-margin and contractual — the cleanest read on what training corpora are actually worth.

description: Reddit content licensing agreement with OpenAI.
exposure_note: Second data-licensing datapoint. Establishes a market rate that content owners across the stack now anchor to.

description: Warehouse automation deployments with large retail and logistics customers.
exposure_note: Placeholder edge — Symbotic's true concentration is Walmart, which is outside the current coverage universe. Flagged for the pipeline to correct.

description: Oracle buys Nvidia systems to build the OCI capacity underlying its AI backlog.
exposure_note: Closes the loop Nvidia -> OpenAI -> Oracle -> Nvidia. Capital that starts at Nvidia returns as Nvidia revenue within about two years.

description: OpenAI agreement to deploy AMD Instinct accelerators at gigawatt scale, with warrants issued to OpenAI.
exposure_note: Third circular-financing structure, and the strongest single validation that a credible second source to Nvidia exists.

description: Electrical distribution, switchgear and UPS into wholesale data center capacity.
exposure_note: Switchgear and transformer lead times are a hard physical gate — capacity cannot energize ahead of this equipment regardless of capital available.

description: Turbines, generators and grid equipment supporting generation and uprate projects.
exposure_note: Gas turbine slots are sold out into the 2030s, which means new dispatchable generation is supply-constrained years ahead of demand.

description: Transmission, substation and renewable EPC services.
exposure_note: Skilled electrical labor is the constraint that converts capex into delivered megawatts. Rate-limits the whole layer above.
